solution: Solution by TINA assisted by AI
We have more than one generator so we are using superposition to calculate voltages/currents.
Names starting with RGenZero refer to very small resistances, used during superposition.
###Processing generator VS2
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (VS2)
R1 and R4 connected in series so Rb0=R1+R4=1kOhm+1kOhm=2kOhm
Re0=RGenZero1=1nOhm=2nOhm
R3 and Re0 connected in parallel so Rd0=R3*Re0/(R3+Re0)=1kOhm*2nOhm/(1kOhm+2nOhm)=2nOhm
Rd0 and R2 connected in series so Rc0=Rd0+R2=2nOhm+1kOhm=1kOhm
Rb0 and Rc0 connected in parallel so Ra0=Rb0*Rc0/(Rb0+Rc0)=2kOhm*1kOhm/(2kOhm+1kOhm)=667Ohm
The total resistance is Ra0 = 667Ohm
Now we calculate the voltage on R1
We know that the voltage between VS2 nodes is 5 Volt.
All voltage generators except for VS2 have been replaced with a short circuit.
All current generators have been replaced with an open circuit.
The components Rb0 and Rc0 connected in parallel. The voltage on Rb0 is 5 Volt because the voltage on Ra0 is 5 Volt
The components R1 and R4 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 5 Volt
R1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R1 is R1/Rb0*5 Volt = 2.5 Volt
###Processing generator VS1
First we calculate the total resistance between the generator nodes (VS1)
R1 and R4 connected in series so Rd1=R1+R4=1kOhm+1kOhm=2kOhm
Re1=RGenZero0=1nOhm=2nOhm

Rc1 and R2 connected in series so Rb1=Rc1+R2=2nOhm+1kOhm=1kOhm
R3 and Rb1 connected in parallel so Ra1=R3*Rb1/(R3+Rb1)=1kOhm*1kOhm/(1kOhm+1kOhm)=500Ohm
The total resistance is Ra1 = 500Ohm
Now we calculate the voltage on R1
We know that the voltage between VS1 nodes is 5 Volt.
All voltage generators except for VS1 have been replaced with a short circuit.
All current generators have been replaced with an open circuit.
The components R3 and Rb1 connected in parallel. The voltage on Rb1 is 5 Volt because the voltage on Ra1 is 5 Volt
The components Rc1 and R2 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 5 Volt
Rc1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on Rc1 is Rc1/Rb1*5 Volt = 10p Volt
The components Rd1 and Re1 connected in parallel. The voltage on Rd1 is 10p Volt because the voltage on Rc1 is 10p Volt
The components R1 and R4 connected in series.
The voltage between this components starting and ending node is 10p Volt
R1 is in the voltage divider so the voltage on R1 is R1/Rd1*10p Volt = 5p Volt
